newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday December 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday December 27.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Officials at the finance ministry are due to meet today to put the finishing touches to a year-end package of measures which form the last part of the 1997 budget. The measures, which aim to raise 4.3 trillion lire, are expected to be approved at a cabinet meeting on Monday (all).

* The government will meet petrol firms representatives today to try and avoid a national four-day strike which has been announced by petrol stations to protest against measures included in the year-end package. As part of the provisions, the government is expected to extend a tax hike on petrol introduced last year and to anticipate some tax payments, including those from petrol stations (all).

* In an interview, opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi says he favours a "centre federation" to put together all "those disappointed in the Olive Tree" coalition. Last Sunday, Italian Renewal, a small centrist party headed by Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, split up in parliament after months of infighting (Corriere della Sera).

* Prime minister Romano Prodi defended the government's proposal to end a long-running pay dispute between metalworkers and industrial employers, saying it was fair and would not fuel inflation. The employers federation Federmeccanica has rejected goverment proposals, which included a 200,000 lire monthly pay rise, as "unacceptable". Labour minister Tiziano Treu wants to resume talks on January 3 (all).

* In an interview EU Commissioner Mario Monti, commenting on the metalworkers issue, says the Italian government should not "recreate the model which has caused so many problems in the past years: a social agreement with the bill paid for by public finances" (La Repubblica).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
